aspects.says: A copy of a rule need not look like one: a map lookup by the raw value decides equality with String.equals, and neither a text search nor a duplicate-code detector finds it.
basis: section:A Copy of a Rule Doesn't Have to Look Like One

aspects.says: A business rule kept in two places agrees with itself until the first fix or change, which reaches only the copy the report named, and the other copy keeps the defect.
basis: section:A Rule Kept in Two Places Gets Fixed in One of Them

aspects.says: Two identical lines are one piece of knowledge only if a change to one must change the other; merging two rules that agree today hands the next change for one of them to both.
basis: section:Identical Lines Are One Rule Only If One Must Change When the Other Does

aspects.says: A key that folds case uses Locale.ROOT, so it is the same on a server whose default locale is Turkish.
basis: section:One Method Decides When Two Names Are the Same, and Every Path Calls It

aspects.says: Whether to merge two equal pieces of code is decided by asking whether one must change when the other does, not by whether their text is equal.
basis: section:Identical Lines Are One Rule Only If One Must Change When the Other Does

aspects.says: The single representation of an equality rule is one method whose result keys the data, so every path, including one added later, goes through it.
basis: section:One Method Decides When Two Names Are the Same, and Every Path Calls It
